decision_table.condition: clean flat scan, one language, product can ship a vendored engine
decision_table.why: on the studio_clean renders it is materially better than our recogniser on BOTH line crops and whole pages -- see the table; ignoring that would be the cherry-pick this file exists to prevent

decision_table.condition: offline web/iOS app, no vendor engine allowed in the bundle
decision_table.why: one 3.6MB ONNX file that runs in onnxruntime-web/WASM; Tesseract means a second wasm runtime plus eng.traineddata (10MB+), and the build gate fails if it returns
we beat all three Tesseract arms on the degraded profiles (handheld_light, jpeg_social) -- Tesseract's binary page segmentation is what breaks there, ours sees a line crop

decision_table.condition: structured fields only (dosage, account number, sort code)
decision_table.why: the 37-symbol alphabet cannot emit punctuation, so '500mg' cannot come back as '500 mg.'; the costs are paid in CER on raw prose, not on the fields the product extracts

decision_table.condition: unreadable input, user must be told
decision_table.why: per-line CTC confidence plus the app's refusal path; a Tesseract pipeline that silently emits confident nonsense on a blurred line has no equivalent gate wired in

decision_table.condition: arbitrary languages, handwriting, tables, or 100+ docs/scan throughput
decision_table.why: we ship ONE 37-symbol English charset trained from scratch and no punctuation; that is a product scope decision, not a capability we claim

limits: 12 synthetic rendered documents (3 doc types x 4 capture profiles, one font, generated by ml/src/capture.py) -- not real photographs; every number here is a synthetic-render number and the template text is the renderer's own ground truth.
Tesseract 4.1.1 (leptonica 1.82.0), eng only, default oem (LSTM); a Tesseract 5 or a different traineddata/language set is a different engine and would need a re-run.

Single detector for all e2e arms: the app's projection-profile detector on the deskewed grayscale. Detection quality caps every line-level number; Tesseract arm (c) uses its OWN layout analysis and is therefore not detector-limited in the same way.

Arm (a) is genuinely unfair to Tesseract and is labelled that way everywhere it appears: the 32px crop is our model's contract, including the 320px width clamp that horizontally squeezes long lines. Arm (b) is the row to quote.

Tesseract is scored with no character whitelist and its sentence-case/punctuation output is then uppercased and whitespace-collapsed on both sides; punctuation is reported as its own column instead of being scored away.

Our engine gets two page variants (raw and CLAHE) because the app preprocesses; the shipped app also runs a restorer and a three-candidate election that this harness does not reproduce, so our harness rows are NOT the app's end-to-end number -- see app_end_to_end_reference.
No confidence thresholding, no lexicon/field-constrained decode and no rejection path is applied to either engine here: this measures raw recognition, not the product's field policy.
Sample size for the field metric is 24 expected fields over 12 documents; per-profile rates are over 3 documents each and should not be read as more than a direction.
